notes: Every terrain sub-mesh is named Terrain_<class>; every built walkable surface is named Walk_<...>. The client turns both into the navigation collision layer the grounding ray tests.
Causeway decks and quays are walk surfaces, so a downward grounding ray under one resolves onto the deck above; the lagoon beneath them is water and is not walkable.

The lagoon floor is terrain and carries the Terrain_ prefix everywhere, including below sea level. That is deliberate: the client casts its grounding ray at every server tile, not only walkable ones, so a region that is mostly water still needs a continuous surface underneath it. Those tiles ground successfully and are marked unwalkable in collision.bin.

channels.note: the ring of deep water around the crown isle

water.note: Shallow/deep tint and caustics are presentation settings for whoever writes the water shader; the GLB ships a flat lit plane.

transform.formula: pixel_x = world_x * scale + offset; pixel_y = world_z * scale + offset

minimap.note: Every Eloria minimap is drawn at one pixel to the metre, so the image's pixel size is the map's size in metres.

lodGroups.notes: Far-tier vegetation only, no ground clutter.
